description: A heart rate study dataset is loaded in JASP (file: '/home/ga/Documents/JASP/HeartRate.csv'). This dataset contains 800 observations from a study comparing resting heart rates between runners and sedentary controls, with participants of both genders. The three columns are: 'Gender' (Female/Male), 'Group' (Control/Runners), and 'Heart Rate' (beats per minute). The researchers suspect that the heart rate data may not meet parametric assumptions and want nonparametric analyses. Perform the following: (1) Run a Kruskal-Wallis test (the nonparametric alternative to one-way ANOVA) with 'Heart Rate' as the dependent variable and 'Group' as the grouping variable. Enable descriptive statistics for this test. (2) Run a Mann-Whitney U test (the nonparametric independent-samples test) comparing 'Heart Rate' between 'Gender' groups (Female vs Male). Enable descriptive statistics and report the effect size for this test. (3) Run Descriptive Statistics for 'Heart Rate' split by 'Group', and enable both boxplots and distribution plots to visualize how heart rate distributions differ between the groups. Save the completed analysis file as '/home/ga/Documents/JASP/heart_rate_nonparametric.jasp'.
